info.description: The public /v1 operations of the Plotwork API, as every Plotwork SDK reads them. Copied from the API by scripts/sync-openapi.mjs; never edited by hand.

post.summary: Say what changed between two versions of a diagram.
post.description: Each side is diagram source, the text of a Plotwork SVG that carries its source, or a hosted link on the picture hosts. Answers with every statement added, removed, renamed, moved to another block, or changed, matched by id rather than by line, with counts, a plain-language summary for a pull request review, and with markdown true a block ready to paste as a comment. A side that gives no source is an answer, not an error. Lays nothing out.

The answer carries every dropped or changed construct as a diagnostic with a hint, the Plotwork validation with icon and group-type suggestions, the outline, and, when render is true, the SVG for each requested scheme. A Mermaid diagram that cannot be read is a normal 200 result with ok false and nothing converted. Prefer this route over converting by hand and then calling the validate, outline, and render routes. To convert every Mermaid fence in a document at once, use the Markdown sync route with convertMermaid set.

post.summary: Check, describe, and draw a diagram.
post.description: Validates the source and, when it is valid, also returns the quality warnings, a plain-text outline, the natural size, and the SVG for the light scheme, the dark scheme, or both. Source with errors is a normal 200 result with valid false, every error with its line, column, and hint, and nothing drawn, so a caller fixes the source and calls again. Prefer this route over calling the validate, outline, and render routes separately: it does the work of all three in one request. Use the single routes only when one fine-grained step is all you need.

post.summary: Change diagram source with small typed operations.
post.description: Applies operations in order (rename, set, add_node, remove, add_edge, remove_edge, move, replace_text) to the source, on every kind, and returns the new source with a result for each operation and the check of the result. Lines no operation touches come back byte for byte. An operation that cannot apply is reported with a hint and skipped, in a normal 200 answer. With svg never (the default) it parses and outlines the result and lays nothing out; with auto or always it also draws it.

post.summary: Publish a diagram and get a link.
post.description: Renders the source and stores the SVG at a public link that cannot be guessed. Only the renderer's own output is stored; there is no field for SVG. The same diagram published again from the same account keeps its link (200, created false) and moves its expiry out. 403 hosting.quota_exceeded says which limit was reached; 413 hosting.too_large says the diagram is larger than the plan hosts.

post.summary: Choose icons for many names at once.
post.description: Takes up to 40 service or product names and an optional cloud provider, and answers for each name with one icon to write as icon=, or, when the name could mean more than one icon, the candidates to choose from. It never guesses: a name that matches nothing is listed as a gap with a neutral fallback. A name with no match is a normal 200 result, never an error. Prefer this route over calling the icon search route once per name; use the search route when you are exploring one idea.

post.summary: Turn a file of another format into a diagram.
post.description: Takes the text of a file and its format: SQL DDL, Prisma, or Drizzle becomes a schema; an OpenAPI 3 document becomes a matrix of who may call each endpoint, or one operation as a sequence; a GraphQL or Protocol Buffers schema becomes a schema; Terraform, Bicep, an ARM template, Pulumi, CloudFormation, the AWS CDK, a serverless.yml, Docker Compose, a Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, Helm, Kustomize, nginx configuration, a Backstage catalog, AsyncAPI documents, a dbt project, a JavaScript workspace, or a GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, or Azure Pipelines pipeline becomes a flow with icons and frames; a Structurizr workspace becomes a C4 diagram of one view; a draw.io file becomes a flow of each page with its icons and frames; CSV or JSON data becomes the chart its shape suits; tree output or a list of paths becomes a tree; a git log becomes a git graph or a timeline. Answers with the Plotwork source, a diagnostic for everything left out with its line and column in the file, the validation, and an outline. A file that cannot be read is a normal 200 result with ok false. It runs no code and fetches nothing, and the text is not stored.

post.summary: Find the sections of a document a picture would help.
post.description: Takes a whole document (Markdown, HTML, or plain text pasted from a wiki) and answers with the sections a picture would help, in document order: the heading and its line, the diagram kind, a one-sentence reason, a confidence, and a starter source drafted from the section's own lists, tables, numbers, and dates. Sections that read well as text, or already hold a diagram fence, are left out, and every cap that left something out is stated in caps. Draws nothing, writes no file, and lays nothing out.

post.summary: Turn a document's diagram fences into pictures.
post.description: Takes a whole Markdown document and its path and answers with the rewritten document (every diagram fence wrapped in a collapsed source section with its picture and a text description), the SVG files to write, and a report per fence with errors that carry line numbers counted in the document sent. With convertMermaid set, every Mermaid fence that can be converted becomes a diagram fence first; the others are left exactly as they were and reported. The route reads and writes no file: the caller writes the returned document and files. A fence with errors is a normal 200 result with status failed in the report. Mode check changes nothing and only reports. Prefer this route over converting, validating, and rendering each fence yourself.

Nothing that fits is a normal 200 result with no matches and a hint for what to try next, never an error. post.description: Takes a pattern id from the find route, a flavour (neutral by default, or aws, azure, gcp), and optional slot values that rename its parts. An unknown id, flavour, or slot, or a value with a quote in it, is a normal 200 result with found false and every problem with its code and a hint, never an error.
